body_md:
## Industry and stock momentum decouple at 1-month horizon; strategy-decay robustness emerges as a new evaluation axis independent of Sharpe; LLM alpha tools risk homogenising and crowding their own signals.

### Industry Momentum vs Stock Reversal: Opposite Signs at 1-Month

Gao, Li, Yuan & Zhou (SSRN abstract_id=6371558, March 2026) show individual stocks display strong 1-month reversal while industry, factor, and characteristic portfolios exhibit short-term momentum at the same horizon — opposite signs from the same look-back window. They identify a 'residual-to-systematic reversal effect': a momentum portfolio's idiosyncratic return negatively predicts its own future systematic return, implying momentum alpha is partly consumed by subsequent reversal of its residual risk.

**Implication:** spawn-candidate: industry-relative mean-reversion — buy stocks whose recent underperformance is idiosyncratic (stock-minus-industry return < 0) while the parent industry ETF is itself in positive momentum, targeting the reversal of residual risk rather than raw price distance from SMA

### Conditional Skip-Month Lifts Momentum Return by ~59%

Dibyam Dikhit (Jan 2026, reviewed by Alpha Architect at alphaarchitect.com/skip-month-mystery/) audited 50 years of industry-level momentum and found the skip-month convention is not a universal rule. When the prior month delivered above-average returns, the 12-1 strategy averaged 2.03%/month; following weak prior months only 1.28% — a 59% spread. High prior-month volatility was independently predictive of weaker subsequent momentum regardless of return direction.

**Implication:** fits existing: momentum-trader — implement regime-conditional skip-month: include t-1 in the formation window only when t-1 return exceeded its 12-month rolling mean AND t-1 realized volatility was below the 12-month median

### Minimum Regime Performance (MRP): Sharpe and Resilience Are Orthogonal

Alexander & Fabozzi (arxiv:2604.08356, April 2026) introduce MRP — the lowest risk-adjusted return a strategy achieved across distinct historical regimes — as a measure of fragility independent of long-run Sharpe. The counter-intuitive finding: strategies with the highest lifetime Sharpe ratios frequently score lowest on MRP, meaning they can collapse entirely in adverse regimes while lifetime stats look strong. They apply this across a broad universe of established factor strategies and provide open-source code for the audit.

**Implication:** fits existing: all strategies — run MRP audit across all 7 strategies; strategies with high Sharpe but low MRP (candidate: commodity-momentum during USD-strength regimes, control-rule-based during sector rotations) are candidates for tighter drawdown stops or regime-off switches

### Regime-Adaptive Continual Learning Beats Static Regime Switching

Pan et al. (arxiv:2606.00143, accepted KDD 2026) propose a portfolio management framework that continuously updates parameters as regimes evolve, explicitly avoiding catastrophic forgetting — the failure mode where a model trained on one regime degrades sharply when a new one begins. In backtests it outperforms static HMM-based regime switchers, which the paper notes are particularly fragile during structural breaks (correlation-structure shifts at crisis onset).

**Implication:** fits existing: macro-aligned — the strategy's yield-curve / DXY signals define regimes statically; augmenting with a lightweight continual-learning layer (e.g. EWC regularisation on a small regime classifier) could improve responsiveness at transition points without full retraining

### LLM Alpha Mining: Homogeneity Accelerates Crowding; SEC Filings Are the Fix

Two concurrent papers expose opposite faces of LLM-based alpha. AlphaAgent (arxiv:2502.16789, Feb 2026) demonstrates that standard LLM factor pipelines produce homogeneous signals — correlated with each other — which accelerate crowding and decay; AST-based diversity enforcement (measuring abstract syntax tree similarity between generated factors) is required to keep signals decorrelated. Separately, arxiv:2603.19944 (Mar 2026) finds raw LLM stock forecasts fail via 'recurring reasoning failures and hallucinated data' but improve materially when grounded in official SEC 8-K / 10-Q filings rather than press coverage.

**Implication:** spawn-candidate: regulatory-filing reactive strategy — parse 8-K / 10-Q filings at EDGAR publication time using a FinBERT or Claude-class model, score sentiment relative to prior filing baseline, and filter positions against existing news-reactive signals to avoid duplication — directly addressable within £10k/strategy retail capital constraints
